answers the parent's open "Cart-level-messages" question directly — see below.**

`Cart-level-messages` (`9323:102373`) carries this `data-rule-annotations` block, verbatim —
this is a real, explicit designer rule, not incidental:

> "Error messages are compiled into one overarching message. This message will be high-level, to
> encourage users to scroll within their cart and identify where they need to resolve the errors.
> If there are multiple errors within cart, the message will call out how many errors the user
> needs to fix before proceeding. When a customer reduces an error, the quantity in the error
> message also goes down; Errors should always stay at the top when multiple messages are
> stacked."

Populated here with: `"There are 2 items in your bag that require action"` — 14px, **regular**
weight (400, "Default/body2"), colour `--alias/color/text/error #9c0000` (= this repo's
`status.error` = `red[500]`, confirmed same hex in `colour.ts`). A 20px `Icon_close` sits inside
a 24px `touchTarget`, **before** the text, gap 8px — this is a **dismiss ("×") icon, not a
warning/error icon** — the banner is closeable, not just a static indicator. Container width
476px, `gap-[4px]` if more than one line ever stacks (only one shown here).

**This is functionally a different component from what commit 8/9 built.** `ZimmInlineMessage`
(built) is a static, per-line-item, non-dismissible display with no aggregation logic. This
Figma mechanism is: cart-wide (not per-item), aggregated/counted, dismissible, and live-updating
as errors resolve. **I see nothing in the plan or handoff that names this mechanism** — worth the
parent checking directly against SFCC-250/272's actual AC text before concluding it's missing
vs. already covered by something not yet obvious to me. Flagging, not concluding.

### The other two message surfaces in this same frame (neither is the banner above)

1. **Per-line-item inline message** — inside each errored `Cart Item`'s `Item Details`, as a
   4th child after `Quantity Selector`, before `Item Actions`. 12px, **regular** weight (400,
   "Default/Caption" — NOT the medium-weight "Default/Caption-strong" the colour+size line
   uses), colour `--alias/color/text/error #9c0000`. Exact copy on this node:
   - Partial OOS: `"Quantity unavailable in this size"` — quantity shown as `3`, stepper icons
     still rendered (can't tell disabled/enabled state from markup alone at this depth).
   - Fully OOS: `"This item in unavailable"` — **verbatim Figma typo, "in" not "is".** `plan.md`
     §4 (B4) quotes this copy as `"This item is unavailable"` — the correct grammar. Either the
     planner/session-notes silently fixed an obvious typo when transcribing (reasonable), or this
     is a genuine live-file/plan divergence. Shipping the corrected grammar is almost certainly
     the right call regardless — flagging for completeness, not as something to "fix" backward
     into matching the typo.
2. **Pre-checkout summary line** — a THIRD, separate message, between the Grand Total row and
   `Cart-button-group`: `"Please review the items in your bag before continuing"` — 14px,
   regular weight, same error red. Not per-item, not the top banner — a third distinct surface.

aggregate banner (dismissible, counted), per-item inline reason (specific), and a pre-checkout
nudge line (generic). Only the middle one has an obvious match in what's built
(`ZimmInlineMessage`, per-item) — the other two don't obviously map to anything named in the plan.

Structurally identical to `default-page-template.md`'s node `9323:65888` (same drawer/header,

above, last two showing the default/no-error state — consistent with "errors stay at the top
when stacked" from the annotation.
